claims.statement: Without external feedback, intrinsic self-correction can lower LLM reasoning performance.

claim_evidence.excerpt: In the context of reasoning, our research indicates that LLMs struggle to selfcorrect their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance might even degrade post self-correction.

comparison_evidence.excerpt: Table 3 caption, GPT-3.5 on GSM8K: Standard Prompting 75.9; Self-Correct (round 1) 75.1; Self-Correct (round 2) 74.7.

claims.search_scope: Abstract claim compared with the Table 3 caption (intrinsic self-correction, no label-based stopping). Table 1 uses the correct label to stop self-correction, which is external feedback, so it is a different condition and was not used for comparison.
claims.reason: Under the same setting, the Table 3 caption shows GPT-3.5 on GSM8K falling from 75.9 with standard prompting to 75.1 after round 1 and 74.7 after round 2 of self-correction. This supports the direction of the claim. Only one model and benchmark row was compared, so the claim's generality is not established here.
